causes.text: Tesla's post-earnings selloff reflected concern that weak core auto profitability was being exposed by ongoing price competition.
The company experienced severe margin compression as regulatory carbon credit sales dropped by more than 50% amid ongoing price competition.
Nvidia rose as additional AI infrastructure deployments around its platform reinforced confidence in demand for its full-stack systems.
The company secured a major government contract with the Department of Energy to build seven new AI supercomputers at national laboratories.
AMD rose as export-license relief reopened a path to ship advanced AI products into China under the new framework agreement.
The export approval aligned with a new US-China framework agreement, averting an estimated $800 million revenue loss for AMD.
UnitedHealth collapsed after suspending its 2025 guidance and unexpectedly replacing its CEO, signaling a deeper-than-expected deterioration in the business.
The company cited higher-than-anticipated medical utilization and rapidly escalating costs inside Medicare Advantage as the core reason the prior outlook was no longer reliable.
Amazon rallied after third-quarter results showed AWS growth re-accelerating, supporting the case that AI investments were translating into cloud demand.
The strong cloud performance proved that the company's aggressive AI investments were yielding tangible market share gains, overcoming previous margin concerns.
Tesla's slide deepened as European demand concerns coincided with investor backlash over Elon Musk's political profile and its effect on the brand.
European registrations data showed Tesla sales plunged 60% in Germany and nearly 40% across the broader European Union.
Rate-sensitive growth stocks gained after Jackson Hole commentary kept the market positioned for a September Fed cut, lifting Tesla with other mega-cap names.
Market participants rotated back into mega-cap tech equities as expectations for a September rate cut remained elevated following the Fed's remarks.
Tesla’s Q4 2024 deliveries of 495,570 missed the Reuters-cited analyst consensus of 503,269, disappointing investors despite setting a quarterly delivery record.
Full-year 2024 deliveries declined 1.1% versus 2023, marking Tesla’s first annual delivery decline since 2015 and reinforcing concerns about slowing EV demand.

causes.text: Nvidia led a semiconductor selloff after DeepSeek's low-cost model suggested frontier AI performance might require fewer premium GPUs than investors had assumed.
The emergence of a highly capable, low-cost open-source AI model raised severe doubts about the sustainability of massive infrastructure investments and future demand for Nvidia GPUs.
